content:
The Maxima & Minima chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Maxima & Minima tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Maxima & Minima

Maximum and minimum values using AM–GM and the vertex of a quadratic — without calculus, the CAT way.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Quadratic ax²+bx+c: vertex at x = −b/2a; min if a>0, max if a<0.
  • For fixed sum, a product is largest when the terms are equal.
  • For fixed product, a sum is smallest when the terms are equal.
  • x + k/x (x>0) has minimum 2√k.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Using calculus where AM–GM is faster (and expected).
  • Getting the max/min direction wrong from the sign of a.
  • Forgetting the equality condition of AM–GM.

faq.q: How do I do maxima–minima without calculus?
faq.a: Use AM–GM for products/sums and complete the square (vertex −b/2a) for quadratics — both are quicker than differentiating for CAT.
